title: Affliction in Zarahemla
summary: In the sixth year of the judges, there are no contentions or wars in Zarahemla. The people are afflicted by losses of brethren, flocks, herds, and grain fields destroyed by the Lamanites. They mourn, believe their afflictions are judgments of God for their wickedness and abominations, and are awakened to remember their duty.

explicit_facts.text: In the sixth year of the judges over the people of Nephi, there were no contentions or wars in Zarahemla.
The people were greatly afflicted by the loss of brethren, flocks, and herds, and by the loss of grain fields trodden under foot and destroyed by the Lamanites.
Every soul had cause to mourn.
The people believed their afflictions were judgments of God because of their wickedness and abominations, and were awakened to remember their duty.

reasonable_visual_inferences: People mourning near damaged grain fields.
unspecified_visual_details: The people's individual appearances and clothing.
The extent and precise appearance of the field damage.
The circumstances of the other losses.

narration.text: there were no contentions nor wars in the land of Zarahemla;
But the people were afflicted, yea, greatly afflicted for the loss of their brethren,
every soul had cause to mourn;

doctrinal_or_story_notes: The judgments of God are the people's reported belief, not a visibly narrated event.
prohibited_inventions: Do not show Lamanites present in this aftermath scene or reenact the earlier destruction.
Do not identify the people as Mulekites.
Do not depict God or a supernatural judgment visibly.
Do not invent identities, deaths, or circumstances for the lost brethren.

title: Baptism in Sidon
summary: The church is established more fully. Alma baptizes many in the waters of Sidon, and they join the church of God. In the seventh year of the judges, about 3,500 people unite with the church and are baptized; peace continues throughout that year.

explicit_facts.text: Many were baptized in the waters of Sidon by Alma and joined the church of God.
Alma had been consecrated high priest over the people of the church by his father Alma.
About 3,500 people united with the church of God and were baptized in the seventh year of the reign of the judges.
There was continual peace throughout that year.

reasonable_visual_inferences: Alma and people being baptized are in the waters of Sidon during a baptism.
unspecified_visual_details: The appearance of the riverbank, clothing, and people being baptized is not specified.

narration.text: many were baptized in the waters of Sidon
there were about three thousand five hundred souls that united themselves to the church of God and were baptized.

doctrinal_or_story_notes: The figure of about 3,500 is reported for the seventh year; the verses do not say all were baptized at Sidon or by Alma.
Alma's father is mentioned in connection with an earlier consecration, not as present at the baptisms.
prohibited_inventions: Do not identify the people as Mulekites or residents of Zarahemla.
Do not depict all 3,500 people in one baptismal moment.
Do not depict Alma's father as present at the baptisms solely because he is mentioned.

title: Pride among members of the church
summary: In the eighth year of the reign of the judges, people of the church begin to grow proud of their riches and wear costly apparel. This afflicts Alma and grieves many teachers, priests, and elders.

explicit_facts.text: In the eighth year of the reign of the judges, people of the church began to grow proud because of their riches, fine fabrics, flocks, herds, gold, silver, and other precious things obtained by their industry.
They began to wear very costly apparel.
This caused Alma much affliction, and many teachers, priests, and elders whom he had consecrated were sorely grieved by the wickedness they saw among their people.

reasonable_visual_inferences: Costly apparel can be visible on some members of the church.
Alma and the grieved church leaders may be shown with sorrowful expressions, without implying they are all present together.
unspecified_visual_details: The appearance of the apparel and the individuals.

narration.text: they began to wear very costly apparel.

prohibited_inventions: Do not identify the people as Mulekites or place the scene in Zarahemla.
Do not identify this Alma as Alma the Elder.
Do not invent speech or imply that Alma and the church leaders witnessed a particular shared event.

title: Contempt and contention
summary: People of the church became prideful, set their hearts on riches and worldly things, scorned one another, and persecuted those who did not believe according to their will. In the eighth year of the judges, contention grew among them. By the year's end, the church's wickedness had become a stumbling block to those outside it, and its progress began to fail.
characters: Those who did not believe according to the will and pleasure of the people of the church

explicit_facts.text: People of the church became prideful, set their hearts on riches and worldly things, scorned one another, and persecuted those who did not believe according to their will and pleasure.
In the eighth year of the reign of the judges, contention, envy, strife, malice, persecution, and pride arose among the people of the church.
By the end of that year, the church's wickedness was a stumbling block to those outside the church, and the church began to fail in its progress.

reasonable_visual_inferences: Scorn and contention could be conveyed through hostile expressions and gestures among people of the church.
unspecified_visual_details: The location, individuals' appearances, and specific forms of persecution are not supplied.

narration.text: there began to be great contentions among the people of the church;

doctrinal_or_story_notes: The stumbling block and failing progress are reported effects, not literal objects or separate visible events.
prohibited_inventions: Do not identify the people as Mulekites or place the scene in Zarahemla.
Do not depict a physical stumbling block or invent a specific act of persecution.

title: Alma sees inequality
summary: At the commencement of the ninth year, Alma sees wickedness in the church, its example leading unbelievers from one iniquity to another, and great inequality among the people. Some despise others and turn their backs on people in need.

explicit_facts.text: At the commencement of the ninth year, Alma saw the wickedness of the church and its example leading unbelievers from one iniquity to another, bringing on the destruction of the people.
Alma saw great inequality: some lifted themselves up with pride, despised others, and turned their backs on the needy, naked, hungry, thirsty, sick, and afflicted.

reasonable_visual_inferences: Alma observes people turning their backs on others in need.
unspecified_visual_details: The location and the people's appearances and identities are not specified.

narration.text: he saw great inequality among the people,

doctrinal_or_story_notes: The effect of the church's example on unbelievers and the resulting destruction are reported, not separate events to depict in this scene.
prohibited_inventions: Do not identify the people as Mulekites or set the scene in Zarahemla.
Do not depict the destruction as occurring in this moment.

title: Some succor the needy
summary: There are lamentations among the people, while others abase themselves, help those in need, share their substance with the poor and needy, feed the hungry, and suffer afflictions for Christ’s sake. They look forward to the prophesied day, retain a remission of their sins, and are filled with joy because of the resurrection of the dead.

explicit_facts.text: There are lamentations among the people.
Others abase themselves, succor those in need, impart their substance to the poor and needy, feed the hungry, and suffer afflictions for Christ’s sake.
They look forward to the prophesied day, retain a remission of their sins, and are filled with joy because of the resurrection of the dead.

unspecified_visual_details: The location, specific goods, and individuals’ appearances are not specified.

prohibited_inventions: Do not identify the people as Mulekites or place the scene in Zarahemla.

title: Alma's sorrow
summary: Alma sees the afflictions of the humble followers of God, the persecutions by the remainder of his people, and their inequality. He becomes very sorrowful, but the Spirit of the Lord does not fail him.

explicit_facts.text: Alma saw the afflictions of the humble followers of God.
The remainder of Alma's people persecuted the humble followers, and Alma saw their inequality.
Alma became very sorrowful, but the Spirit of the Lord did not fail him.

reasonable_visual_inferences: Alma appears sorrowful while observing the afflictions.
unspecified_visual_details: The location, clothing, and physical appearances are not described.

doctrinal_or_story_notes: The Spirit's support is stated, but no visible appearance is described.
prohibited_inventions: Do not identify the setting as Zarahemla or give the unnamed groups other identities.

title: Nephihah receives the judgment-seat
summary: Alma selects Nephihah, a wise man among the church elders, and gives him power to enact and enforce laws according to the voice of the people. Nephihah is appointed chief judge and sits in the judgment-seat. Alma retains the office of high priest.

explicit_facts.text: Alma selected a wise man among the elders of the church and gave him power, according to the voice of the people, to enact and enforce laws.
The man was Nephihah. He was appointed chief judge and sat in the judgment-seat to judge and govern the people.
Alma delivered the judgment-seat to Nephihah but retained the office of high priest.

reasonable_visual_inferences: Nephihah can be shown sitting in the judgment-seat.
unspecified_visual_details: The judgment-seat’s design and the location’s appearance are not specified.

narration.text: Now this man’s name was Nephihah, and he was appointed chief judge; and he sat in the judgment-seat to judge and to govern the people.

doctrinal_or_story_notes: Nephihah receives the civil office, while Alma retains the office of high priest.
prohibited_inventions: Do not depict an unmentioned ceremony or crowd.

title: Alma Delivers Up the Judgment-Seat
summary: At the commencement of the ninth year of the judges, Alma delivers the judgment-seat to Nephihah and confines himself wholly to the high priesthood and testimony of the word. He intends to go among the people of Nephi to preach and call them to remember their duty.

explicit_facts.text: Alma delivered the judgment-seat to Nephihah at the commencement of the ninth year of the reign of the judges.
Alma intended to go among the people of Nephi to preach the word of God, stir them to remember their duty, and confront pride, craftiness, and contention through pure testimony.
Alma confined himself wholly to the high priesthood and testimony of the word, according to revelation and prophecy.

reasonable_visual_inferences: Alma and Nephihah may be shown together for the transfer of the judgment-seat.
unspecified_visual_details: The setting and physical manner of the transfer are not described.
The appearances and clothing of Alma and Nephihah are not described.
